DMR_Regulation_18.full_name: Driven Machinery Regulations â€“ Regulation 18: Lifting Machines and Lifting Tackle
DMR_Regulation_18.enabling_legislation: Occupational Health and Safety Act (Act 85 of 1993)
key_requirements: All cranes must be examined and subjected to a performance test by a registered Lifting Machinery Inspector (LMI) before first use
Re-examination and performance test required every time a crane is dismantled and re-erected at a new location
Annual examination at intervals not exceeding 12 months thereafter
Ropes, chains, hooks, attaching devices, sheaves, brakes, and safety devices to be examined by a competent person every 6 months
Maximum safe working load (SWL) must be clearly and permanently marked on the crane
Safety devices (brakes, load limiters, anti-two-block systems) must be functional at all times
Records of all inspections, tests, and examinations must be kept on-site

LMI_requirements.definition: Lifting Machinery Inspector â€“ a person registered by the Engineering Council of South Africa (ECSA) under the Engineering Profession Act (Act 46 of 2000)
LMI_requirements.role: Mandatory for all crane load tests and commissioning inspections in South Africa
requirements: Must be registered with ECSA under the Specified Scope (Lifting Machinery Inspector) pathway
Must demonstrate knowledge of erection, load-testing, and maintenance of the specific crane type
Must be assessed by an ECSA Registration Committee and found competent for specific machine types
Application requires: completed ECSA forms, qualifications, experience reports, developmental questionnaire, inspection and load test reports, and referee reports

crane_operator_certification.governing_body: Transport Education Training Authority (TETA) accredited under SAQA unit standards
requirements: All crane operators must hold a TETA-accredited qualification aligned to the applicable SAQA unit standard for the crane type
Crane operator licenses expire every 2 years; renewal requires recertification
Minimum entry requirement: Grade 9/ABET 4 (NQF Level 1), minimum 18 years of age
Mobile crane operators: Grade 10 / NQF Level 2 equivalent + valid heavy vehicle driver's license (Code C or EC)
Assessment: 20% written (theory, safety, operational procedures) + 80% practical (hands-on supervised competence demonstration)
Training providers must be accredited with QCTO

accredited_providers.name: HRETD (Heavy Rescue Equipment and Training Division)

lift_plan_requirements.description: A formal Lift Plan is required under the OHS Act and DMR 18 for all non-routine and complex lifts. Lift plans become mandatory above certain risk thresholds and are required by most large clients as a contractual condition.
thresholds_requiring_engineer_signoff: Lifts exceeding 80% of the crane's rated capacity at any radius
Lifts involving hazardous materials or restricted headroom
Lifts on public roads or near overhead powerlines
All critical lifts as defined by the client's safety management system
lift_plan_requirements.sign_off_requirement: Lift plans for complex or critical lifts must be reviewed and signed off by an ECSA-registered Professional Engineer (PR Eng) or Professional Engineering Technologist (PR Tech Eng) with relevant lifting experience
lift_plan_contents: Load weight, centre of gravity, and rigging attachment points
Lift radius, boom angle, and capacity chart extraction
Exclusion zones and site risk assessment
